abstract: This paper presents evidence for the demand‐driven propagation of job losses in the context of the United States during the Great Recession. Using county‐level tradable job losses driven by aggregate shocks as an instrument, it shows that retail and restaurant (R&R) employment fell by 0.37% for every 1% of job loss in the rest of the county's economy. The finding is not driven by the house price decline or by credit supply problems. Moreover, the spillover is more severe for R&R industries that are most affected by consumer demand shocks during the Great Recession, which strengthens the argument for the demand‐driven propagation of job losses.
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title:
Demand‐Driven Propagation of Job Losses: Evidence from the Great Recession

abstract: We examine how the eleven GICS sectors of the S&P 500 respond to U.S. non-farm payroll (NFP) surprises across 209 informative monthly releases (2008–2025). Against a 250-day market-model benchmark, payroll news is priced through relative sector repricing rather than a uniform market move. On positive surprises, Industrials outperform and Real Estate and Utilities underperform the market; these effects survive family-wise correction at the 10% level across 22 sector-by-sign hypotheses. Symmetry is rejected only for Industrials, at the 10% level: it gains on good news without losing on bad news, although its positive- and negative-surprise slopes do not differ. The cross-section lines up with interest-rate sensitivity: the two-year Treasury yield rises on positive and falls on negative surprises, and pre-event sector interest-rate betas predict announcement-day abnormal returns with opposite-signed effects whose symmetry is not rejected. The Utilities effect loses significance once the yield change enters the benchmark, whereas the Real Estate effect does not. Results are robust to alternative estimation windows, factor-augmented benchmarks, controls for unemployment, wage and revision surprises, and a calendar-based exclusion of confounded release days. The evidence is consistent with a discount-rate channel concentrated in rate-sensitive sectors; a cash-flow channel is not directly identified.
title: Payroll surprises and relative sector repricing in the S&P 500: the role of interest-rate sensitivity

abstract: The response of labour supply is a key dimension of the relationship between credit conditions and labour market outcomes. Using panel data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) covering 2014–2022, this study examines how provincial credit growth shapes household labour supply. We find that a one-percentage-point increase in the credit growth rate is associated with a 0.17-percentage-point increase in employment probability and a 0.13-hour increase in weekly working hours, with household debt, particularly mortgage debt, serving as an important channel. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that the relationship is stronger among less educated, married, male, and flexibly employed individuals. This study provides new empirical evidence that provincial is positively associated with household labour supply largely through greater indebtedness.

title: Debt-driven workforce: how credit growth shapes household labour supply
title_zh: 债务驱动的劳动力：信贷增长如何影响家庭劳动供给

abstract: Using matched firm-level and daily meteorological data from China (2001–2020), we examine how sustained high-temperature exposure shapes firms’ digitalization strategy (DS). We develop a multi-period framework in which firms can continuously adjust their DS over time. High-temperature exposure may shape DS through two channels: a drive channel, by increasing the operating losses that digitalization can mitigate and thus raising its marginal return; and a constraint channel, by reducing the financial resources available for digitalization. Thus, the net effect of high temperatures on DS is theoretically ambiguous. Relative to the 12°C–15°C baseline, we find that high temperatures significantly reduce firms’ DS over medium- to long-run windows: a one-standard-deviation increase in cumulative exposure to temperatures above 30°C over a 9-year window (approximately 87.52 days) is associated with a 0.16-unit decline in DS (mean = 0.68). The negative effect attenuates for larger firms and under improved financing conditions, while substantial industry heterogeneity is observed. This article enriches the literature on climate adaptation, calls on managers to consider environmental factors in strategic decision-making, and provides empirical evidence for the consistency between long-run economic interests and ecological interests.

abstract: As geopolitical rivalry intensifies and pressures toward deglobalization grow, the systemic vulnerabilities of global production networks have become increasingly evident. Global value chains are shifting from an efficiency‐first model toward one that places greater emphasis on both efficiency and security, accelerating the regional reorganization of cross‐border production. Using industry‐level panel data covering China and 20 Asia‐Pacific partner countries from 2000 to 2022, this paper examines how cross‐national industrial spillovers affect regional value chain resilience. The results show that cross‐national industrial spillovers significantly strengthen China's regional value chain resilience. Mechanism analysis indicates that these spillovers operate through two complementary channels: they reduce bilateral institutional frictions and improve soft infrastructure, while also deepening China's digital embeddedness in partner countries and strengthening hard infrastructure connectivity. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the resilience‐enhancing effect is concentrated in technology‐ and knowledge‐intensive industries and is particularly pronounced for partner countries with higher levels of political trust and greater geographic proximity. These findings provide new empirical evidence on the regional restructuring of global value chains and suggest that emerging economies can strengthen resilience to external frictions and production disruptions by developing regional production networks with politically trusted and geographically proximate partners.

abstract: Although China has rapidly expanded its renewable energy capacity and its fleet of electric vehicles (EVs), flawed market mechanisms continue to hinder the practical implementation of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. Insufficient economic incentives have resulted in low user engagement, leaving the vast energy storage potential of EVs largely untapped. To bridge the gap between policy objectives and market realities, this paper proposes a policy-oriented market mechanism built around a novel carbon credit trading framework. This innovative carbon credit policy is integrated with renewable energy contracts, demand response programs, and ancillary services, enabling EVs to function as dispatchable distributed energy resources through virtual power plants (VPPs). Using empirical load and mobility data from Hubei Province, a policy-targeted economic analysis validates the mechanism, its economic viability, and its overall effectiveness. The results show that the proposed carbon credit trading mechanism introduces a critical revenue stream, effectively offsetting the rigid operational costs faced by EV users while actively encouraging V2G participation. Moreover, coupling carbon value with policy reforms that allow battery swapping stations to participate in mid- and long-term electricity trading significantly shortens investment payback periods and improves the internal rate of return (IRR). Overall, the study suggests that embedding the carbon value of flexible resources into electricity market rules represents the most critical policy pathway for unlocking V2G potential and facilitating large-scale renewable energy integration.

abstract: Agriculture is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions but has largely been exempt from stringent climate change mitigation policies, often due to concerns about resistance from the sector. With Denmark introducing the world’s first CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 e) tax on agricultural emissions, this paper provides representative evidence of farmers’ beliefs about its impacts and examines whether providing expert-predicted impacts can causally influence these beliefs and acceptance of the tax. Using a randomized survey experiment with 981 Danish farmers, we find a widespread overestimation of the tax’s impacts on production, employment, and land value, with 94–97 % of farmers expecting the impacts to be up to three times larger than expert-predicted estimates. Providing an expert-predicted impact reduces these perception gaps, with effects varying according to the tax’s stringency, size of belief gaps, and farm characteristics such as size and type. However, our results also indicate that, in some cases, belief updating may be muted or even contrary to the information provided, consistent with behavioral theories beyond the Bayesian framework. We also find that the belief revisions can translate into greater acceptance of the tax, although these effects vary with tax stringency, initial belief gaps, and farm characteristics. Our findings suggest that designing acceptable climate policies for agriculture may require not only expert information but also targeted communication and complementary measures that account for farmers’ diverse characteristics and perceptions.
title: Farmers’ beliefs about the impacts of a CO2e tax on agriculture and their acceptance of the tax: A randomized survey experiment
title_zh: 农民对农业二氧化碳当量税影响的认知及其税收接受度：一项随机调查实验

abstract: We study the political economy of transport infrastructure placement and its long-term impact, exploiting quasi-random variation in political factors. Using unique data from XIX-century Italy and deploying a regression discontinuity design, we focus on close races to show that towns in marginal districts supporting winning candidates were more likely to be reached by a railway. Using alignment with the government as a natural instrument for infrastructure placement, we then show that over the following century, services - rather than manufacturing - grew faster in connected municipalities. Our results also indicate that political allegiances likely helped towns with lower growth prospects.
journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
title: Pork, Infrastructure and Growth: Evidence from the Italian Railway Expansion,
title_zh: 猪肉、基础设施与增长：来自意大利铁路扩张的证据

abstract: L'essor des investissements dans les technologies d'intelligence artificielle suscite des inquiétudes quant à l'éventualité d'une bulle spéculative. Cet article soutient que l'essor des années 1920 et la Grande Dépression offrent des enseignements utiles. Au cours des années 1920, l’innovation en matière de procédés a connu une croissance rapide, tandis que l’innovation en matière de produits stagnait. À son tour, l’innovation en matière de procédés a alimenté un boom des investissements fondé sur des anticipations de demande future. Lorsque ces anticipations ne se sont pas concrétisées, une forte contraction s’en est suivie. Ainsi, l’optimisme et la prospérité des années folles aident à expliquer le déclenchement de la Grande Dépression et constituent un avertissement pour le boom actuel de l’intelligence artificielle.
authors: Harold Cole, Stefano Cravero, Jeremy Greenwood
title: L'essor avant l'effondrement : des « années folles » à la Grande Dépression
title_zh: 崩溃前的繁荣：从“疯狂年代”到大萧条

abstract: Population aging is increasing demand for senior residential tourism (SRT), making effective siting of SRT complexes an important land-use planning challenge. Yet existing approaches face three connected challenges: preserving stakeholder welfare, incorporating active-aging values, and combining intelligent interaction with deterministic, spatially traceable decisions. Therefore, this study develops SilverSmart, a human-centered spatial decision framework for SRT complex siting. Stakeholder-specific utilities keep the welfare of Older adults, Government, and Enterprise visible, while acceptability screening and normalized weighted Nash bargaining coordinate conflicting preferences. Additionally, a 24-criterion synergistic evaluation system broadens aging-oriented land valuation by incorporating active living, cultural participation, destination experience, and longer-stay conditions. During formal decision execution, generative artificial intelligence (AI) supports interaction and interpretation, while formal rankings remain deterministic and linked to geographic information system (GIS) geometries. SilverSmart achieved the best mean rank across 12 planning tasks (1.54; Friedman p = 6.92 × 1 0 − 8 ). It significantly outperformed three conventional multicriteria baselines, while remaining comparable to weighted overlay under highly aligned preferences. Under controlled conflict, bargaining produced a jointly acceptable compromise as stakeholder optima diverged. Moreover, removing two participation-oriented criteria shifted ranks by 88.68 positions on average and substantially changed the cross-county composition of the Top-20, demonstrating that active-aging values materially reshape spatial priorities. All 1014 candidates retained numerical-to-geometric traceability, and multi-scale tests revealed resolution-dependent changes in mapped priorities. Together, SilverSmart connects stakeholder coordination, active-aging land valuation, and spatial accountability in a transparent process, providing a practical basis for pre-decision screening, stakeholder negotiation, and spatially defensible SRT land-use choices.
title: Human-centered land-use planning for senior residential tourism complexes: Stakeholder-preserving Nash bargaining with accountable artificial intelligence support
title_zh: 以人为本的养老旅游综合体土地利用规划：利益相关者保护的纳什 bargaining 与可问责人工智能支持

abstract: Official quarterly US GDP estimates begin in 1947; earlier quarterly histories must be reconstructed using annual benchmarks and historical indicators. To investigate uncertainty in these reconstructions, this paper systematically compares specifications drawn from the literature for reconstructing quarterly GDP during 1919–1946. The comparison evaluates predictions on concealed postwar quarters and separates variation across specifications from coefficient uncertainty within a model. Reconstruction choices matter, but their effects differ across episodes. Across 58 reconstruction specifications, the interquartile range of estimated peak-to-trough declines is 30.9–31.6% for the Great Depression, compared with 6.6–7.8% for 1937–1938. A reconstruction that augments the production-regression approach of Balke and Gordon (1986) with the Denton allocation used by Ramey and Zubairy (2018) has the lowest prediction error. Industrial production supplies information about quarterly movements, while annual accounts constrain the resulting path. Richer indicator panels, additional expenditure detail and more flexible relation ships do not improve on this reconstruction’s predictive accuracy. Its estimated 7.07% decline in 1937–1938 is milder than the approximately 10.5–10.6% declines in those published reconstructions. The reconstruction matches all six NBER recessions, but dates the first contraction two quarters earlier, from 1919Q3 to 1921Q1 rather than 1920Q1 to 1921Q3; its peak is the earliest allowed by the dating window.

title: Prewar US business cycles under uncertainty: reconstructing quarterly GDP before 1947

abstract: We study the role of middlemen as an exchange technology in international production networks. Using matched transaction-level data between Chilean importers and Argentine exporters, we show that about 40 percent of imported intermediate inputs are brought in by domestic intermediaries rather than final producers. We document three important patterns: (i) even large foreign suppliers trade with few Chilean importers, implying high per-relationship costs; (ii) many suppliers sell both directly and indirectly through middlemen; and (iii) middlemen pay roughly 5 percent lower prices for identical products. These facts motivate a model where trade involves per-customer costs, and intermediation arises to economize on them. The model replicates observed patterns and indicates that removing intermediation reduces productivity by 1.8 percent, corresponding to nearly half the loss from closing the border to trade. Indirect exchange doubles the productivity effects of trade liberalization and lowers industry concentration. Intermediation thus emerges as a key, overlooked driver of efficiency in developing economies.
title: Middlemen as an exchange technology in international production networks
title_zh: 中间商作为国际生产网络中的交换技术

abstract: This study examines how the location of public charging stations (PCS) shapes the spatial equilibrium of a monocentric urban economy. We develop a linear urban model in which commuters endogenously choose vehicle type (conventional or electric), charging mode (public or home), and residential location. We show that the PCS location affects these choices, which in turn determine urban spatial structure, traffic-related emissions, and social welfare. We find that placing the PCS in non-ideal locations may exacerbate urban sprawl, reduce electric vehicle adoption, and lower social welfare. We derive closed-form solutions for the optimal PCS location under alternative policy objectives and quantitatively illustrate how deviations from the optimum affect equilibrium outcomes.
title: On the optimal location of public charging stations in a monocentric city
title_zh: 单中心城市公共充电站的最优区位

abstract: We measure investors’ short- and long-term stock-return expectations using both options and survey data. These expectations at different horizons reveal what investors think their own short-term expectations will be in the future, or forward return expectations. Across data sources, investors’ forward return expectations are countercyclical, especially when measured as forward risk premiums. This countercyclical variation is, however, excessive, as changes in forward return expectations are too large relative to subsequent realized short-term expectations. The excess variation in forward return expectations can help account for a meaningful share of the stock-price declines during the global financial crisis and the COVID-19 crisis. (JEL G10, G12, G40)
title: Forward Return Expectations
title_zh: 远期收益预期

abstract: We decompose cross-sectional differences in the level of price-earnings ratios using professional forecasts. High price-earnings ratios are accounted for by both low expected returns and overly high expected earnings growth. The magnitudes and timing of the comovements between prices, earnings growth, and returns are consistent with gradual learning rather than expectations being highly sensitive to recent realizations. Earnings growth surprises do not translate 1-1 into one-period returns but instead are gradually reflected in returns over time. A structural risk-premium model incorporating constant-gain learning about mean earnings growth replicates our findings and generates realistic dispersion and persistence in price-earnings ratios. (JEL G11, G12, G14, G40)
title: The Cross-section of Subjective Expectations: Understanding Prices and Anomalies
title_zh: 主观预期的横截面：理解价格与异象

abstract: We estimate the supply-side effects of climate change on firm sales by exploiting variation in local average temperature across suppliers of the same client. A 1°C increase in temperature leads to a 2.5% decline in annual sales. This effect is nonlinear, with stronger effects among suppliers in regions with the largest temperature increases and in cooler regions. Manufacturing and heat-sensitive industries are more affected, consistent with a reduction in labor productivity and labor supply when local temperatures rise. Nondiversified and financially constrained firms are also more affected, supporting the importance of operational and financial flexibility in adapting to climate change.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Does Climate Change Affect Firm Sales? Identifying Supply Effects
title_zh: 气候变化会影响企业销售额吗？识别供给效应

abstract: Using regression discontinuity and difference-in-differences designs to compare prices of California homes across a new wildfire risk zone boundary, I identify null effects in the immediate vicinity of the new risk zone boundary. In contrast, prices of homes newly assigned to a riskier zone drop by 5.7% further away from the new risk zone boundary. These findings suggest that households do not respond to the risk salience triggered by the new risk zone assignment. Instead, they update their risk beliefs in response to rezoning in a way that is consistent with the actual wildfire risk.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Does the Salience of Climate-Related Risk Affect Asset Prices?
title_zh: 气候相关风险的显著性会影响资产价格吗？

abstract: Initial sequence estimators are commonly used to estimate Monte Carlo standard errors for reversible Markov chains used in Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations. Despite their widespread use and subsequent methodological extensions, they are known only to be asymptotically conservative, with consistency still an open question. We address this gap by investigating the statistical properties of the initial positive sequence estimator. Leveraging a nonnegativity property of sums of adjacent autocovariances from reversible Markov chains, the initial positive sequence estimator is obtained by summing sample autocovariances until a sum of adjacent sample autocovariances becomes negative. We characterize the convergence behavior of this random truncation point. We also propose an alternative initial sequence type estimator based on a modified truncation rule. For both estimators, we establish consistency and derive bounds on rates of convergence, showing that, under geometric ergodicity, both converge to the asymptotic variance no slower than the near-parametric rate of (log n)/n 1/2. Finally, through empirical studies using both simulated and real-world data, we validate our theoretical findings and compare the empirical performance of the two initial sequence-type estimators with the standard overlapping batch mean estimator.
title: Consistency and convergence rate bounds of initial sequence type variance estimators for reversible Markov chains
title_zh: 可逆马尔可夫链初始序列型方差估计量的相合性与收敛速率界

abstract: Life‐cycle wage growth varies substantially across countries. We study the firm productivity distribution's role in a random‐search model with learning and labor‐market frictions, estimated for Brazil, Colombia, and the United States. Brazil has a long left tail of low‐paying firms, and Colombia has a highly compressed firm ladder. Replacing each country's firm distribution with that of the United States closes most of the cross‐country gap in wage growth, raising Brazil's relative wage growth from 73 to 103 percent and Colombia's from 52 to 115 percent. The results are robust to alternative distributional assumptions and additional sensitivity checks.
title: Life‐Cycle Wage Growth and Firm Productivity in Developed and Developing Economies
title_zh: 发达国家与发展中国家的生命周期工资增长与企业生产率

abstract: Why do recycling industries emerge rapidly in some resource markets but remain persistently marginal in others, even when recycling technologies are economically feasible? This paper develops a dynamic model of an exhaustible-resource monopolist interacting with a competitive fringe of recycling firms to examine how resource endowments shape the emergence of secondary supply. The model incorporates an endogenous waste stock: current extraction creates future recyclable waste, thereby affecting both the future scale of secondary supply and its entry conditions. We show that abundant reserves can induce the extractor to sustain a high-extraction path that deters recycling entry through limit pricing, generating prolonged dependence on virgin material supply. By contrast, when endowments are limited, continued extraction more rapidly erodes scarcity rents, reducing the incentive for exclusion and leading the extractor to accommodate secondary supply earlier. The analysis characterizes the resulting equilibrium transitions between virgin extraction and recycling. It thereby identifies a distinct deterrence mechanism: whereas related models may delay recycling by slowing depletion or waste accumulation, an incumbent can instead expand extraction to keep prices sufficiently low to deter secondary entry.
title: Recycling, endowments, and market power in exhaustible resource industries
title_zh: 可耗竭资源行业中的回收、禀赋与市场势力

abstract: This paper examines how reserve-backed stablecoins influence Treasury markets and financial intermediation. Using high-frequency Ethereum blockchain data matched to intraday returns on the BIL ETF that tracks short-term U.S. Treasuries, I show that large Tether issuances are followed by an increase in BIL prices in the following hour, reflecting a combination of forward-looking market expectations of sustained Treasury demand and Tether’s reserve deployment into short-term Treasuries. A complementary daily frequency analysis corroborates this pattern. A quantitative macro-finance model with capital-constrained banks and stablecoin issuers embeds this Treasury demand channel and reveals nonlinear amplification as the sector expands, highlighting how stablecoin growth can reshape safe asset pricing, bank balance sheets, and financial stability.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
source_issue: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
title: Macro-Financial Impact of Stablecoin’s Demand for Treasuries
title_zh: 稳定币对国债需求产生的宏观金融影响

abstract: Growth in trade of perishable foods has significantly increased global access to fresh foods, but important trade-offs arising from perishability are not captured in standard trade models. In this paper, we develop a model of age-related product freshness that places importer logistics choices at the center of the analysis. The model highlights order size and order frequency as key trade margins, alongside the nonlinear pricing that arises from scale economies in trade. Importers determine freshness through their order-size and order-frequency choices, balancing a cost–quality trade-off. This has important implications for understanding the quality effects of growth, innovation, and trade policy. For instance, while innovations in cold-chain technology directly improve freshness, their overall effect depends on importers’ logistics choices, which also influence the carbon emissions associated with perishable trade. Fresh seafood is one of the most successful categories in the global expansion of fresh food trade. Using transaction-level data on Norwegian seafood exports from the world’s largest exporter of fresh seafood, we document that order-size discounts are important. We use the model to evaluate how reductions in perishability and protective tariffs affect trade outcomes and product freshness.
title: Logistics and product quality in perishable food trade
title_zh: 易腐食品贸易中的物流与产品质量

abstract: We present a two-sector growth model in which a representative agent invests in fossil fuel-based energy and renewable energy. These differ in capital intensity and project duration: fossil investments have lower upfront costs and more front-loaded payoffs; clean investments are more capital-intensive and have longer cost-recovery periods. We show that a negative economic shock (such as an energy supply shock or recession) leads to both cuts in total investment and to a shift in the composition of the remaining investment toward fossil fuel projects. This delays the clean energy transition, even if renewable energy is cost-effective on a levelised cost basis, implying a role for policies to sustain clean investment during recessions. We discuss how this mechanism can be amplified by higher interest rates, pro-cyclical climate policies, perceived risk, and financial frictions.
journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
source_issue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
title: Energy shocks and the climate transition
title_zh: 能源冲击与气候转型

abstract: US Treasuries have long been the benchmark dollar safe asset, and the convenience yield they command is the price the world pays for dollar liquidity. This column shows that the convenience yield on ten-year Treasuries relative to corporate bonds has collapsed from around 60 to 10 basis points since 2019, while the premium on repo has held near 90. Repo, not the Treasury, is now the highest-convenience dollar safe asset. The same shift helps explain why the dollar has been losing ground as the global reserve asset even as domestic convenience yields hold up.
title: Repo is the new dollar safe asset
title_zh: 回购是新的美元安全资产

abstract: In international affairs, what a country does depends on its own interests and on what its partners do. This column uses data on political institutions and UN voting to recover the network of geopolitical influence. The network tracks major shifts in international politics since the 1960s and reveals three notions of power: autonomy, control, and the ability to shape the game. Across all countries, the US has the most autonomy but China has the most control. Domestic political change in the US or China moves other countries the most, as the network transmits it furthest.
authors: Ernest Liu, Bennett Smith-Worthington, Stephen Redding, David Yang
china_relevance_reason: 标题、摘要或元数据包含中国相关关键词
title: A network approach to geopolitics

abstract: It is now well established that the COVID-19 pandemic had a devastating and unequal impact on student achievement. Test score declines were disproportionately large for historically marginalized students, exacerbating preexisting achievement gaps. In this paper, we use longitudinal student-level NWEA MAP Growth test data to estimate differences in test score declines for students at different points on the prepandemic test distribution. We examine whether these widening gaps occurred within schools and districts – between high- and low-achieving students – or between schools and districts that served more versus fewer lower-achieving students before the pandemic. We find that while lower-achieving students experienced greater incidence of learning loss during the pandemic (relative to higher-achieving peers), these differences are significantly attenuated with the inclusion of school and district fixed effects. Decomposition analyzes show that roughly three-quarters of the widening in math achievement occurred between schools, indicating that students with lower prior achievement disproportionately attended schools where average losses were larger.
title: Pandemic learning loss by student baseline achievement: extent and sources of heterogeneity
title_zh: 疫情学习损失与学生基线成绩：异质性的程度与来源

abstract: Cost-effective and scalable soil testing tools can play an instrumental role in guiding agricultural decisions and policies, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa, where declining soil fertility poses a serious threat to productivity. Laboratory tests of soil samples, which provide the most accurate measures of soil properties, remain costly and challenging to scale in the context of national surveys or programs. To test and validate alternative approaches to soil measurement, the World Bank launched the Uganda Climate, Land Area, and Soil Study project. This paper evaluates the accuracy and scalability of three soil testing tools (the AgroCares Scanner, the Palintest kit, and the Sonkir pH meter) as well as two publicly available soil maps (Innovative Solutions for Decision Agriculture and SoilGrids), against laboratory-based soil measurements conducted by the Center for International Forestry Research and the International Centre for Research in Agroforestry. While differences in soil parameter estimates may be expected to vary across testing methods, understanding the nature and magnitude of the divergence in estimates from those measured using established laboratory approaches is critical for practitioners and analysts seeking to leverage soil analyses to inform policy and program design. The paper finds that the soil tools – except the Sonkir pH meter, which performs poorly – provide only moderately adequate predictions of soil properties, and both soil maps fail to capture sample variation. These findings highlight key trade-offs in accuracy, cost, and scalability and offer practical guidance for scaling soil monitoring strategies in Uganda and similar contexts.
journal: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
publisher: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
series: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
source_name: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
title: Scanning for Soil Health: Assessing the Accuracy and Scalability of Innovations for In-Situ Soil Measurement
title_zh: 扫描土壤健康：评估原位土壤测量创新的准确性与可扩展性

abstract: This study examines how diaspora communities affect foreign direct investment flowing into Economic Community of West African States countries. It uses data on international migration to represent the size of the diaspora and estimates their savings. The analysis covers 14 countries from 2005 to 2020, using system generalized method of moments and feasible generalized least squares methods. The study finds that members of the diaspora living in Europe help bring more foreign direct investment to their home countries, while the diaspora in Asia has a smaller and sector-specific effect, helping attract foreign direct investment in extractive industries. The diaspora in North America has little impact, and migration within Africa does not significantly affect foreign direct investment. Importantly, strong home country institutions—like good governance, anti-corruption efforts, and political stability—make the positive effects of the diaspora even greater. The study also finds that former British colonies attract more foreign direct investment than former French or Portuguese colonies, likely because of stronger property rights under common law systems. Although most foreign direct investment continues to target the extractive sector, the study underscores the importance of strengthening institutions and implementing targeted policies in countries of origin. These measures can help harness the potential of diaspora networks to boost investment, particularly in sectors beyond natural resources that can drive structural transformation and quality jobs creation.
journal: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
publisher: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
series: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers

abstract: Reliable electricity supply is essential for firms to maintain production continuity and efficiency. Using daily newspaper text, we construct a city-level Electricity Supply Reliability Index (ESR) for China and match city-year electricity conditions to firm-level data from the National Tax Survey during 2009–2015. We find that a one-standard-deviation decrease in ESR is associated with an approximately 0.97% decline in firm total factor productivity (TFP). The relationship holds across a range of robustness tests. We further document two dimensions of structural adjustment. First, output and intermediate inputs become relatively more concentrated in cities with more reliable electricity supply. Second, deteriorating ESR is associated with greater within-industry differentiation: a one-standard-deviation decrease in ESR is associated with an approximately 0.16-percentage-point increase in the industry revenue share of firms in the top 10% of the operating-revenue distribution and a 0.003-percentage-point decrease in that of firms in the bottom 10%. Moreover, lower ESR is associated with lower TFP among follower firms, whereas the corresponding estimate for profit-defined industry leaders is statistically insignificant. These findings indicate that unreliable electricity supply is associated not only with lower average productivity but also with differences in the spatial distribution of production and firm performance within industries.

abstract: How can an institutional shock alter the economic value of productive capabilities? The shock can change the viability of activities in which capabilities are deployed, shifting derived demand and revaluing those capabilities. Capabilities are more exposed to revaluation when their economic value depends more strongly on the affected institutional conditions, while revaluation is amplified by high activity substitutability and low capability transferability. Demand shifts can generate labor-market disequilibrium when established deployment contracts faster than alternative productive capacity can expand. Adverse capability revaluation can also make institutions themselves an object of adjustment. Agents facing larger losses, limited labor-adjustment opportunities, and greater institutional-adjustment capacity are more likely to seek institutional restoration or modification. Institutional shocks can therefore set in motion a recursive process: they revalue capabilities and reorganize labor markets, while the resulting gains and losses create incentives for endogenous institutional adjustment.
title: Institutional Shocks and Capability Revaluation: Labor-Market Disequilibrium and Endogenous Institutional Adjustment
title_zh: 制度冲击与能力重估：劳动力市场非均衡与内生制度调整

abstract: This paper sets forth a tractable incomplete markets monetary model with money and other nominal safe assets including a long-maturity government bond. Money serves as a medium of exchange whereas all safe assets allow agents to self-insure against risks. Portfolio demand for these assets can serve as a nominal anchor that determines the price level. The paper examines and contrasts monetary transmission mechanisms involving different monetary policy instruments and links it to classic monetary results, including the Tobin effect, Sims’ stepping on a rake effect, Sargent-Wallace unpleasant monetarist arithmetic, Wallace neutrality of open market operations, and the Friedman rule.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
source_issue: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
title: A Monetary Model with Money and Safe Assets
title_zh: 一个包含货币与安全资产的货币模型

abstract: We study how the precision with which merger-specific efficiencies are assessed affects the incentives to invest in such efficiencies before the merger review. With binary investment and an exogenous cutoff, greater precision strengthens investment incentives. We then show how the analysis extends to continuous investment choice and Bayesian approval. A more rigorous merger assessment can therefore encourage efficiency creation.
title: Merger control and investment: The role of efficiency assessment

abstract: Financial over-the-counter markets often lack both pre-trade transparency (visibility of current quotes) and post-trade transparency (disclosure of past trades), which raises concerns about their efficiency. We propose a dynamic trading model with adverse selection to study both forms of transparency. We find that post-trade transparency improves welfare relative to the opaque market but is dominated by pre-trade transparency; moreover, in markets that are already pre-trade transparent, introducing post-trade transparency does not generate further gains and can sometimes reduce welfare. To test the robustness of these conclusions, we use a mechanism-design approach to characterize the optimal trading mechanism in our framework.
title: Optimal Transparency in Over-the-Counter Markets
title_zh: 场外市场中的最优透明度
